newsitem.title: UK: ScotPower jumps as forecasts 19 pct div rise.
newsitem.headline: ScotPower jumps as forecasts 19 pct div rise.

text.p: Shares in multi-utility Scottish Power brushed aside a weak FTSE 100 trend and jumped four pence to 345.5 pence on the market opening, after forecasting a robust 19 percent rise in annual dividend, analysts said.
"That was well above the trend," noted Andy Stone, utilities analyst at brokers Daiwa.

Another analyst, who declined to be named, noted that Scottish Power, which posted half year pretax profits of 188 million stg before reorganisation costs, had also beaten his expectations of 182 million stg.
Analysts welcomed news that Scottish Power would improve pretax profits at its Southern Water subsidiary by 52 million stg per year and cut 2,050 jobs.
"The company is cutting costs and putting its neck on the line with a dividend forecast," the second analyst noted.

Scottish Power, which has been keen to sell the idea that one company can provide competitive prices for water, electricity and gas, forecast a full year dividend of 18.5 pence, a rise of 19 percent, after lifing the first half payout one penny to 6.17p.
